items.title: Tinubu calls for peaceful election in Osun, charges security agencies to protect voters, INEC officials
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission and the security agencies to ensure a peaceful and transparent election in Osun State. The people of Osun State will go to the polls on Saturday, August 15, 2026, to elect their governor in an election where 15 candidates are contesting. Among them are the incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, the All Progressives Congress, APC, candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, and the African Democratic Congress, ADC candidate, Hon. Najeem Salaam. President Tinubu also charged the electorate in Osun State to come out to discharge their civic responsibility and eschew any act that could disrupt the peaceful conduct of the election, while assuring the people of their safety before and after the polls. “As the people of Osun State head to the polling units to elect who will govern them in the next four years, I call on the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure orderly conduct of the election. “The election must be transparent, free and fair. I urge INEC to ensure the integrity of the process,” the President said. “INEC must use this last off-cycle election as a test case to demonstrate to Nigerians their full preparedness for the 2027 polls,” he added. “I have charged the Inspector-General of Police and other heads of security outfits taking part in the election to provide maximum security at polling units. No room should be allowed for troublemakers to disrupt the process. “Electoral officials and voters must be protected so they can perform their civic duties without fear or intimidation. “Voters should feel confident to go out in their numbers to vote for the candidate of their choice as all measures necessary to ensure a peaceful, free and fair election have been put in place. “Our elections must be credible, and the outcome of the Osun Governorship election must reflect the will of the people,” Tinubu declared. items.title: Tiv, Arewa youths laud Tinubu over creation of Army Division in Benue
items.description: ..hold joint peaceful rally By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Tiv Youth Council, TYC, Worldwide and the Arewa Youth Assembly, AYA, have commended President Bola Tinubu for approving the creation of the 5 Division of the Nigerian Army, with headquarters in Makurdi, Benue State, describing the development as a major boost to security in the North Central region. The youth groups gave the commendation on Friday, during a joint peaceful rally organised in Makurdi to appreciate President Tinubu, the Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, and the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Waidi Shaibu, for the establishment of the new Army division. In an address delivered on behalf of the TYC Worldwide, its Secretary, Emmanuel Katseen, said the creation of the division was a significant response to years of security challenges confronting Benue communities. Katseen said the state had endured armed attacks, kidnappings, banditry, militia activities and communal conflicts, resulting in loss of lives, destruction of property, displacement of residents and disruption of agricultural activities. According to him, “for decades, Benue State has faced serious security challenges, including armed attacks, kidnappings, banditry, militia activities and communal conflicts. These have led to loss of lives, destruction of property, displacement and disruption of farming activities, threatening our status as the Food Basket of the Nation.” He said the TYC had consistently advocated stronger security measures to protect communities and enable displaced residents to return to their homes and farms, describing President Tinubu’s approval of the 5 Division as evidence of his administration’s commitment to the security and welfare of Nigerians, while also commending the military leadership for strengthening security operations in the region. He said the new division would strengthen military command and control in Benue and the North Central, improve rapid response to security threats, protect farming communities and facilitate the restoration of agricultural activities. The Tiv youth leader also expressed optimism that the division would create opportunities for youth recruitment and empowerment in the Nigerian Army, while stimulating socio-economic development through improved infrastructure and increased economic activities. The council pledged its cooperation with the new division and other security agencies, promising to support credible intelligence sharing, mobilise youths to embrace peace and discourage the harbouring or protection of criminals. It also called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, community leaders, youth organisations and residents across Benue and the North Central region to support the military and other security agencies in their efforts to restore lasting peace. Similarly, the Publicity Secretary of the Arewa Youth Assembly, Aliyu Muhammad, described the creation of the 5 Division as a historic development and a demonstration of political will by the Tinubu administration. Muhammad, who spoke at the rally, said the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions and the establishment of the 5 Division in Benue represented a major elevation of the state’s strategic importance in the country’s security architecture. “Today is not a day for long grammar, but for loud gratitude, for the expansion of the Nigerian Army, from eight to 12 divisions and the establishment of the 5th Division in Benue State by President Tinubu,” he said. According to him, Benue had historically hosted Army brigades but had now been elevated to the status of a full division headquarters, describing the development as evidence that the President was committed to fulfilling his campaign promises, particularly on security. Muhammad said the strategic location of the division would enable it to respond not only to security threats in Benue but also to challenges in neighbouring Nasarawa and Kogi states, as well as other parts of the North Central. While urging the Federal Government to provide adequate funding and modern military equipment to enable the new division to discharge its responsibilities effectively, he said, “we must also add our voices to call on the President to ensure adequate funding for this new Division and the provision of modern equipment to aid its work. The Arewa youth leader, who expressed confidence that the presence of the new division would contribute significantly to tackling insecurity in the region and restoring public confidence, also commended the Chief of Defence Staff and Chief of Army Staff for their leadership, courage, experience and expertise in military operations, saying their efforts had placed the country on a path of renewed confidence. Muhammad further charged the General Officer Commanding the new 5 Division to maintain close engagement with the people of Benue, particularly the youths, and ensure that the host community remained an important partner in the division’s operation. “Carry the people of Benue along as your host community, especially the youths, and act always in their best interest,” he added. The post Tiv, Arewa youths laud Tinubu over creation of Army Division in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Paix et sécurité en Afrique : le journaliste Mohamed Cissé au Forum sous-régional de la jeunesse en Côte d’Ivoire
items.description: La 7ᵉ édition du Forum sous-régional de la jeunesse sur la paix, la sécurité et les droits de l’homme s’est ouverte ce mercredi 12 août 2026 à Bouaké, en Côte d’Ivoire. Réunissant les autorités locales, des partenaires techniques et financiers ainsi que la jeunesse influente de la sous-région et du Sahel, cet événement majeur compte une forte délégation guinéenne composée d'une trentaine de jeunes leaders. Parmi les figures clés mobilisées à Bouaké figure Mohamed Cissé, journaliste, administrateur général du média Avenirguinee et commissaire général du Concours Universitaire de l'Entrepreneuriat de Guinée. Participant actif aux travaux, le journaliste guinéen a tenu à souligner l'importance cruciale de la thématique centrale axée sur la prévention des conflits. « Je voudrais d'abord remercier les organisateurs de cette importante activité qui réunit la jeunesse de la sous-région et du Sahel. Le thème axé sur l’implication de la jeunesse dans la prévention des conflits est d’autant plus important qu'il met les jeunes face à leurs responsabilités. La majorité de la population africaine est jeune ; les jeunes ne devraient pas être en marge des décisions fondamentales en faveur de la paix, de la sécurité et de la promotion des droits de l’homme. D’où l’importance de ce rendez-vous majeur », a déclaré Mohamed Cissé. En marge des réflexions stratégiques, la première journée a été marquée par une marche blanche symbolique, organisée pour porter haut les messages de cohésion sociale et de tolérance. Un moment fort et lourd de sens, particulièrement dans la cité de Bouaké. « Vous savez que nous sommes à Bouaké, une ville qui a connu la rébellion. Mais, en voyant cette population aujourd'hui, on sent qu’elle a tourné cette page douloureuse et qu’elle est pleinement engagée dans la promotion de la paix. Cette marche est une manière de prouver que la jeunesse de la sous-région et du Sahel a compris la nécessité du pardon et qu’elle s’implique désormais dans la promotion du vivre-ensemble », a ajouté l'administrateur général d'Avenirguinee. Après cette entame symbolique et studieuse, la deuxième journée du forum sera marquée par l'ouverture officielle du marché artisanal, illustrant l'intégration culturelle et socio-économique des jeunes participants. L’article Paix et sécurité en Afrique : le journaliste Mohamed Cissé au Forum sous-régional de la jeunesse en Côte d’Ivoire est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Adeleke camp condemns release of APC Assembly candidate allegedly found with gun
items.description: The Imole Campaign Council has commended the Nigerian Navy for what it described as professionalism and neutrality in Osun State, while condemning the reported release of an All Progressives Congress House of Assembly candidate allegedly arrested with a gun. In a statement issued on Friday by its spokesman, Pelumi Olajengbesi, the council said its attention had been drawn to “the arrest and subsequent controversial release of an All Progressives Congress member, Babatunde Festus Komolafe, who is also the APC House of Assembly candidate for Atakumosa East/West Local Government Area.” According to the statement, Komolafe, popularly known as BFK, was apprehended by naval personnel in his hometown of Ifewara on Thursday. The council alleged that “during a routine search conducted by men of the Nigerian Navy, the APC candidate was arrested alongside his supporters while travelling in a campaign vehicle reportedly belonging to the APC after a gun was allegedly discovered in the vehicle.” It said the arrest had become public knowledge after a video of the suspects circulated widely on social media. “The arrest is no secret, as a video showing the suspects has since gone viral and attracted public outrage,” the statement read. The campaign council further claimed that the suspects were released shortly after their arrest due to pressure from senior APC figures. “However, we gathered reliably that the arrested APC candidate and his co-perpetrators were immediately released following pressure from APC top goons,” it stated. The statement added that “a news outlet even chronicled how the naval officer in charge was forced to release the suspects and asked to step aside.” Despite its criticism of the release, the council praised the conduct of the armed forces during the ongoing governorship election campaigns. “The Imole Campaign Council commends the men and officers of the Nigerian Armed Forces, especially the Nigerian Navy, for their neutrality and professionalism since the commencement of the governorship election campaigns,” the statement said. It added, “The men and officers of the Nigerian Armed Forces have been proactive in arresting troublemakers regardless of party affiliation. Special salute to our gallant troops!” The council, however, insisted that releasing a suspect allegedly found with an unauthorised firearm was dangerous. “That said, the release of a suspect who was caught with an unauthorised gun is unacceptable. It sends the wrong signal to political criminals whose pastime is killing and maiming,” the statement declared. The group linked the incident to what it described as the APC’s past conduct in Osun State. “This is particularly alarming because of the APC’s antecedents in Osun. Just two weeks ago, the police launched an attack on military personnel to rescue five APC hoodlums, including the notorious APC thug, Asiri Eniba, arrested by the Nigerian Navy for shooting sporadically in Ile-Ife with pump-action guns,” it alleged. The council called on the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to intervene. “We call on the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to look into this grave injustice and punish the suspects,” the statement said. It concluded, “No politician is above the law, and no political thug should be released to keep fomenting trouble.” The post Adeleke camp condemns release of APC Assembly candidate allegedly found with gun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Finances publiques : 12,8 milliards de dirhams de recettes supplémentaires grâce à l’impôt sur les sociétés
items.description: À fin juillet 2026, les recettes tirées de l’impôt sur les sociétés (IS) ont connu une forte progression, illustrant le dynamisme des ressources fiscales de l’État. Selon les statistiques publiées par la Trésorerie générale du Royaume (TGR), ces recettes ont augmenté de 21,8 % par rapport à la même période de l’année précédente, soit un gain supplémentaire de 12,8 milliards de dirhams. Cette évolution s’inscrit dans un contexte de hausse globale des recettes ordinaires de l’État, qui ont progressé de 8,3 % à fin juillet. Cette amélioration est portée principalement par la bonne tenue des recettes douanières, en hausse de 13,3 %, ainsi que des recettes fiscales intérieures, qui ont enregistré une augmentation de 12,8 %. À l’inverse, les recettes non fiscales ont reculé de 23,2 % sur la période. Les recettes douanières ont bénéficié d’une progression généralisée de leurs principales composantes. Les droits de douane ont augmenté de 14,1 %, générant 1,3 milliard de dirhams supplémentaires. La taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) à l’importation a, pour sa part, progressé de 12,7 %, soit une hausse de 4,4 milliards de dirhams. La taxe intérieure de consommation (TIC) appliquée aux produits énergétiques a enregistré une augmentation de 11,8 %, représentant un supplément de 1,3 milliard de dirhams. La TGR relève également une hausse de 15,4 % de la TIC sur les tabacs manufacturés, équivalant à 1,2 milliard de dirhams additionnels. Les autres taxes intérieures de consommation ont, quant à elles, progressé de 20,3 %, soit une augmentation de 394 millions de dirhams. Du côté de la fiscalité intérieure, les recettes ont augmenté de 18,6 milliards de dirhams à fin juillet 2026 par rapport à leur niveau observé un an auparavant. Outre la forte progression de l’impôt sur les sociétés, cette évolution est alimentée par une hausse de 2 % des recettes de l’impôt sur le revenu, représentant 855 millions de dirhams supplémentaires, ainsi que par une augmentation de 11,1 % de la TVA intérieure, soit 3,1 milliards de dirhams de plus. En parallèle, les recettes non fiscales ont enregistré un recul de 7,219 milliards de dirhams, correspondant à une baisse de 23,2 %. Cette diminution s’explique principalement par la contraction des transferts des comptes spéciaux du Trésor vers le budget général, qui se sont établis à 10,685 milliards de dirhams contre 14,470 milliards de dirhams à la même période de 2025. Les recettes liées aux opérations d’allègement de la dette ont également fortement diminué, passant de 3,080 milliards de dirhams à 198 millions de dirhams. Sur le plan des dépenses, les charges globales du Trésor ont augmenté de 13,3 % à fin juillet. Cette progression résulte notamment de la hausse de 14,3 % des dépenses de biens et services. Les dépenses de personnel ont progressé de 10,4 %, tandis que les autres dépenses liées aux biens et services ont enregistré une hausse de 19,9 %. Les charges d’intérêts de la dette ont, de leur côté, augmenté de 2,7 %. Les dépenses de compensation ont connu une accélération marquée, avec une hausse de 65 %, atteignant 10,7 milliards de dirhams, soit 4,2 milliards de dirhams de plus qu’à fin juillet 2025. Les remboursements, dégrèvements et restitutions fiscaux ont également progressé de 13,2 %. L’investissement public poursuit par ailleurs sa progression. Les dépenses d’investissement émises ont augmenté de 10,2 %, passant de 65,4 milliards de dirhams à fin juillet 2025 à 72 milliards de dirhams à fin juillet 2026. Cette évolution est attribuée à une hausse de 14 % des dépenses des ministères et de 6,2 % des dépenses relevant des charges communes. Au terme des sept premiers mois de l’année, l’exécution de la loi de finances fait apparaître un solde ordinaire positif de 4,5 milliards de dirhams. Ce résultat demeure toutefois inférieur à celui enregistré un an auparavant, où l’excédent ordinaire atteignait 16,5 milliards de dirhams. Malgré cette situation, les comptes du Trésor affichent un déficit global de 48,2 milliards de dirhams à fin juillet 2026. The post Finances publiques : 12,8 milliards de dirhams de recettes supplémentaires grâce à l’impôt sur les sociétés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Camp vacances Faso Mêbo à Fada N’Gourma : Dix jours d’épreuves et d’apprentissage pour 525 « bâtisseurs de demain »
items.description: Le « Camp vacances Faso Mêbo » a débuté, hier jeudi 13 août 2026, à Fada N’Gourma. Pour le compte de la 6 e Région militaire qui, administrativement, regroupe les régions du Goulmou, de la Sirba, de la Tapoa et du Nakambé, ils sont 525 jeunes campeurs qui seront formés et sensibilisés, durant dix jours, aux valeurs du patriotisme, du civisme, de la solidarité… Proclamée le 1 er avril 2025 par le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, La Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) repose sur des valeurs cardinales telles que le patriotisme, le civisme, la solidarité et la cohésion sociale, entre autres. Conscientes de l’importance et de la nécessité d’inculquer ces valeurs aux citoyens dès le bas âge, les autorités ont initié, en 2025, le Camp vacances Faso Mêbo. Avec pour slogan : « Camp vacances Faso Mêbo, je m'instruis et je participe à la construction de ma nation. La Patrie où la Mort nous Vaincrons !», l’édition 2026 de cette initiative présidentielle a été lancée, hier jeudi 13 août, à Fada N’Gourma. Pour le compte de la 6 e Région militaire, ils sont au total 525 jeunes campeurs qui prennent part à l’initiative. Le lieutenant-colonel Aboubacar Dadijan, commandant la 6e Région militaire et parrain de l’évènement aux jeunes campeurs : « La discipline doit être votre boussole». Cette nouvelle aventure a débuté avec la montée des couleurs, faite par les campeurs eux-mêmes, en présence des autorités militaires, paramilitaires et administratives. Après cette étape, ils ont participé à la confection de pavés et à la plantation d’arbres. Il s’agit, là, d’un avant-gout des activités qui vont rythmer leur quotidien jusqu’au 24 août prochain. En effet, selon le lieutenant-colonel Aboubacar Dadijan, commandant la 6 e Région militaire, commandant d’armes de la place de Fada N’Gourma et parrain de l’évènement , les campeurs participeront tout au long de leur séjour aux travaux de Faso Mêbo et à des séances de plantation d’arbres. Aussi, a-t-il indiqué, ils seront initiés à la géopolitique, formés et sensibilisés au civisme, au patriotisme, à la discipline et au vivre ensemble, sans oublier les exercices d'éducation physique, militaire et sportive. « Tout cela leur permettra d’acquérir du savoir, du savoir-être et du savoir-faire », a-t-il affirmé. « R especte z scrupuleusement les consignes » Le représentant du DG de Faso Mêbo, le sous-lieutenant Inoussa Koutou, a exhorté les campeurs à respecter scrupuleusement les consignes " data-large-file="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-879x1024.jpeg" class="size-full wp-image-167567" src="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2.jpeg" alt="" width="1595" height="1858" srcset="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2.jpeg 1595w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-258x300.jpeg 258w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-879x1024.jpeg 879w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-768x895.jpeg 768w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-1319x1536.jpeg 1319w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-361x420.jpeg 361w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-150x175.jpeg 150w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-300x349.jpeg 300w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-696x811.jpeg 696w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3.JPG-2-1068x1244.jpeg 1068w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1595px) 100vw, 1595px" /> Le représentant du DG de Faso Mêbo, le sous-lieutenant Inoussa Koutou, a exhorté les campeurs à respecter scrupuleusement les consignes En outre, le camarade lieutenant-colonel Dadijan a noté que cette initiative présidentielle vise à préparer les enfants à affronter avec courage et détermination les défis de leur époque. En sa qualité de parrain régional du Camp vacances Faso Mêbo, le camarade lieutenant-colonel Dadijan a prodigué un chapelet de conseils empreints de sagesse à ses filleuls. « La discipline doit être votre boussole. Il a exhorté également chaque campeur à cultiver l’amour du travail bien fait et à chérir sa patrie à travers de simples actes de solidarité, de civisme et de respect des symboles de la république. L’officier militaire s’est ensuite adressé aux enfants en ces termes :« Je vous encourage donc à saisir la chance qui vous est offerte, car vous n'êtes pas ici seulement en vacances, vous êtes à l'école de la vie, de la citoyenneté et du patriotisme. Profitez de chaque instant, de chaque seconde de ce camp pour apprendre, pour grandir, pour tisser des liens de fraternité solide ». items.title: Les Gafam, les Batx et nous (Par Aly DIOUF)
items.description: Le géant américain du numérique Meta a été convoqué, le mercredi 12 août, devant le tribunal fédéral d’Oakland, en Californie, dans un procès majeur consacré à la protection des mineurs sur Facebook et Instagram. À l’origine de la procédure, les États de la Californie, du Colorado, du Kentucky et du New Jersey. Ils agissent au nom d’une coalition de 29 États américains qui accusent le groupe de Mark Zuckerberg d’avoir délibérément conçu Facebook et Instagram pour favoriser une utilisation compulsive chez les adolescents ; violant ainsi les lois de protection des consommateurs et la législation fédérale protégeant les données des enfants.Les plaignants dénoncent le défilement infini, la lecture automatique des vidéos, les notifications, les recommandations personnalisées ou encore de système de « likes ». Selon les procureurs, ces fonctionnalités ont été pensées pour maintenir les jeunes le plus longtemps possible sur les plateformes, afin notamment d’augmenter leur exposition à la publicité. L’accusation s’appuie également sur les révélations de Frances Haugen, ancienne employée de Facebook devenue lanceuse d’alerte en 2021. Elle avait fait « fuiter » des milliers de documents internes, les « Facebook Files », montrant notamment que l’entreprise était bien au courant des dégâts et des risques de ses réseaux sociaux sur la santé mentale des adolescents tout en niant cette réalité en public. La procédure intervient alors que Meta fait déjà face à de nombreuses plaintes de familles, de collectivités et d’établissements scolaires. En 2025, Meta a été condamné au Nouveau-Mexique et en Californie. Loin d’être une simple formalité, ce nouveau procès est pris au sérieux par la multinationale. Le groupe de Menlo Park conteste fermement ces accusations. L’entreprise affirme avoir renforcé ses dispositifs de protection des mineurs et soutient que l’usage problématique des réseaux sociaux ne peut être assimilé à une addiction médicale. Elle estime également que la santé mentale des jeunes dépend de nombreux facteurs et ne saurait être imputée à une seule entreprise. Après la sélection du jury, les débats doivent commencer le 18 août et durer environ six semaines. La sanction maximale théorique évoquée par les plaignants atteint 1 400 milliards de dollars, un montant proche de la capitalisation boursière de Meta ou encore le Pib de pays comme les Pays-Bas ou l’Arabie Saoudite, les 18e et 19e économies mondiales. Mais dans ce procès, l’enjeu dépasse largement ce montant. Les États réclament des changements dans le fonctionnement de Facebook et Instagram pour les utilisateurs mineurs. Ailleurs en Chine, connue pour l’importance notoire des Batx (Baidu, Alibaba, Tencent, Xiaomi), la protection des enfants sur Internet est devenue un chantier majeur de la politique numérique. Beijing impose directement des règles aux plateformes, aux fabricants de smartphones et aux services numériques. Depuis 2025, un « mode mineur » permet notamment de basculer simultanément les applications d’un téléphone dans un environnement conçu pour les jeunes utilisateurs. Il prévoit des contenus adaptés à l’âge, des recommandations davantage contrôlées et des mécanismes destinés à limiter le temps passé en ligne. À partir du 1er mars 2026, les plateformes ont le devoir de mieux identifier et limiter les contenus susceptibles de nuire à la santé physique ou psychologique des mineurs. Ces contenus ne doivent notamment plus être mis en avant par les fils de recommandation, les recherches tendance ou les fenêtres promotionnelles. Il faut y ajouter aussi les obligations spécifiques appliquées aux plateformes comptant un très grand nombre de jeunes utilisateurs ou exerçant une influence importante sur eux. En attendant, ici en Afrique, on subit l’influence des Gafam (Google, Apple, Facebook, Amazon, Microsoft) et des Batx (Baidu, Alibaba, Tencent, Xiaomi). aly.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: A Cold War Movie That Gives Too Much Credit to Ronald Reagan
items.description: Americans do not know enough about the Cold War, and much of what they think they know is wrong. After the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991, Republicans took a victory lap, rightly noting that the Soviet collapse was unimaginable when President Ronald Reagan first took office. Liberal critics, however, argued—also rightly—that the Soviet Union was a decaying, economically crippled giant by the time Reagan was inaugurated. In the years since, explanations of the ending of that great conflict have been reduced to the equivalent of partisan bumper stickers: We crushed the Kremlin in the arms race , or The U.S.S.R. imploded without any pressure from the West . In October 1986, Reagan and Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev met to discuss nuclear-arms control in Reykjavik, Iceland. At the time, I was a young scholar in Washington, training in Soviet affairs and international relations at Georgetown University and working at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. (I was also a two-time Reagan voter.) When the Reykjavik meeting took place, no one was looking ahead to the collapse of the Soviet Union; Kremlin watchers were, mostly, relieved to see a Soviet general secretary and an American president talking with each other. The Brink of War , a new film released nationwide today, tries to bring texture and detail to those two days in Iceland. The movie relies on transcripts and other documents from the time, along with interviews with a former secretary of state, the late George Shultz (to whom the movie is dedicated). The film is a welcome corrective to the liberal orthodoxy about Reagan—specifically, that he was a disconnected simpleton who didn’t understand the complexities of the arms race. But it leans too much in the opposite direction: It is too kind to the Gipper, and takes too many liberties with the historical record. As a viewing experience, The Brink of War is a better film than the only other movie about the summit, a 1987 British production titled Breakthrough at Reykjavik . But that’s because the earlier movie (now no longer available, as far as I can tell) was more accurate—and perhaps, for some viewers, more boring. The diplomats who met in the middle of the night thought they were ridding the world of nuclear arms, and that story has plenty of drama, but The Brink of War forgoes those details in favor of needless melodrama and a focus on fewer personalities. [ Read: The thin line between biopic and propaganda ] The title itself is misleading. The world was not on the brink of war in late 1986. Soviet-American tensions were much higher, and the risk of war much greater, during Reagan’s first term, which were perhaps the most dangerous years of the Cold War since the Cuban missile crisis. In the early ’80s, the Soviet Union was led by Yuri Andropov, a former KGB chief. In 1983 alone, Reagan gave his “Evil Empire” speech and announced the start of his missile-defense plan, the Strategic Defense Initiative; the Soviets shot down a civilian Korean airliner (killing a U.S. congressman); and the Americans overthrew a Marxist regime in Grenada. Andropov died in 1984, and Gorbachev took more than a year to gain power while the Kremlin stumbled along under the caretaker regime of the grievously ill Konstantin Chernenko. Gorbachev’s arrival cooled some of these tensions. Almost a year before Reykjavik, Reagan and Gorbachev met in Geneva, where they issued a joint announcement that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.” This was an important moment: Gorbachev, still consolidating power, was taking a risk by bucking anti-American hawks back in Moscow and standing with Reagan to join him in officially ruling out nuclear war as a rational instrument of policy. By the time the two men met in Iceland, they were both determined to reduce their nations’ stockpiles of nuclear weapons. For Gorbachev, this reflected both a sincere belief and an economic imperative. The Soviet Union was struggling with the costs of boneheaded decisions such as the invasion of Afghanistan and the deployment of new and extremely threatening Soviet nuclear weapons in Europe. Reagan, despite his reputation among his critics as a warmonger, was actually an abolitionist when it came to nuclear weapons, and on this, he and Gorbachev were of one mind. Both men had earlier made dramatic proposals to rid the world of nuclear arms. These were roundly dismissed in each other’s capitals as propaganda, but as it turned out, Reagan and Gorbachev were completely serious. The meeting foundered because of Reagan’s commitment to SDI, but the Reykjavik summit, despite its failure to reach any agreements, nevertheless suggested to the two leaders that they agreed about important things. The Brink of War gets much of this right, but it portrays Reagan as highly prepared and Gorbachev as somewhat nervous. In reality, Reagan was concerned about the meeting, and at the start he relied on notes and cards he had in front of him. One of Gorbachev’s first observations when they met was about all the paper in front of his American counterpart; Reagan at one point dropped all of his notes and had to shuffle through them to get back on track. The film also shows Reagan confidently teasing his negotiating team about being Democrats, which was probably done so that the movie could make the summit seem like a bipartisan effort. It’s true that a few Reaganites were once Democrats, such as the negotiator Richard Perle, but this was not a team of liberals and conservatives. Perle was so distrustful of arms control with the Soviets that his nickname in Washington in the ’80s was the “Prince of Darkness.” Soon the two leaders took up the proposal first discussed in Geneva for a 50 percent cut in Soviet- and American-weapons stockpiles. Reagan and Gorbachev, in the course of their discussion, agreed to eliminate all nuclear weapons, a move that surprised both delegations. The idea of full abolition—beloved by both leaders but not part of the Reykjavik agenda—was an improvised moment, almost an accident, and not some premeditated masterstroke (as the movie implies) by Reagan. This sudden change drove hours of unexpected negotiations. Both sides, in a very short time, got remarkably close to a major nuclear deal, because their bosses, both Soviet and American, wanted one. These American negotiators do not get much attention in the film; likewise, the Soviets, starting with Gorbachev himself, get unfair treatment in The Brink of War . The Soviet boss huddles in the bathroom with his wife, hiding from the KGB, as if he were doing something illegal and not presenting positions he’d already raised among Soviet leaders. The film also depicts Gorbachev as something of a drama queen during the meetings, slamming the table and raising his voice. At one point, when Reagan suggests sharing missile-defense technology, Gorbachev stands up and whines about how America will not even share dairy technology so that the Soviets can provide milk to their children. Reagan did make that missile-defense technology offer, and Gorbachev did in fact dismiss it. What Gorbachev actually said, however, according to records from the meeting, was more restrained: “Excuse me, Mr. President, but I do not take your idea of sharing SDI seriously. You don’t want to share even petroleum equipment, automatic machine tools or equipment for dairies.” This was a kind of sarcastic zinger from the real Gorbachev. But in any case, no Soviet leader would complain to an American president about hungry Soviet kids. It would have been especially out of character for Gorbachev, who Shultz later recalled was not whiny but rather “brisk, impatient, and confident, with the air of a man who is setting the agenda and taking charge of the meeting.” Other Soviets appear as central-casting scary Communists. The Soviet Foreign Minister Eduard Shevardnadze is played as a glowering, skeptical presence by a darkly handsome English actor. The real Shevardnadze looked more like a white-haired professor, and he supported Gorbachev’s proposals. Likewise, Marshal Sergei Akhromeyev, the senior military officer who led the Soviet negotiators, is portrayed as a difficult, stiff military man, but American negotiators, especially Paul Nitze, later spoke of him with great admiration as smart, flexible, and someone the Americans could trust. The Brink of War also presents Reykjavik as something of a guy’s poker party. Men conduct the work in the movie, but in real life, some of the important negotiations with the Soviets were led by the veteran diplomat Rozanne Ridgway, who does not appear in the film. The two most important women in the film are the wives, Raisa Gorbacheva and Nancy Reagan. Raisa is presented as a chic, smart adviser to her husband. Nancy, who stayed in Washington, is Ronnie’s faithful booster, but she also unfairly comes across as a catty flake, envying Raisa and telling the president that the stars are aligned for a successful summit. Nancy Reagan, fearful of losing her husband, did indeed consult an astrologer after Reagan was shot. But Karen Tumulty, The Washington Post ’s chief political correspondent and the author of a definitive biography of Nancy, told me that Nancy was angry in October 1986 not because she felt upstaged, but because her husband’s advisers had told her that Iceland was not a “summit” and therefore that Raisa would not be there. A scene where Nancy tells Ron about the position of Mars, Tumulty added, “strikes me as preposterous.” The supreme error in The Brink of War , however, is that it wanders too far from the history of the event in order to depict a successful summit. In life, the two leaders agreed about ridding the world of nuclear weapons, but they both left Iceland full of gloom and bitterness. A deal to eliminate nuclear arms dissolved when Reagan insisted that testing for SDI had to continue. Gorbachev, hamstrung by demands from hard-liners back in Moscow, was equally intransigent that no deal could be made so long as SDI was in the works. The summit-that-was-not-a-summit failed. As the Reagan biographer Max Boot told me, both Reagan and Gorbachev left “furious and disappointed.” Tumulty cites Nancy Reagan as saying later that it was clear to her, watching from afar, that her husband, “pale” and with his “teeth clenched,” was extremely angry as he said goodbye to Gorbachev. According to declassified Soviet transcripts released years later, as the two leaders stood outside waiting to leave, Reagan accused Gorbachev of not wanting a deal in the first place, adding that he didn’t know when they would meet again. (“I don’t either,” Gorbachev said.) Ken Adelman, one of Reagan’s aides at the meeting, later wrote that Reagan, during that final conversation, recalled Gorbachev saying, “I don’t know what else I could have done.” Reagan answered: “I do. You could have said yes.” None of this makes its way into The Brink of War. Instead, the film makes much of Reagan trying to get a visa for the sister of Mstislav Rostropovich, a Soviet musical maestro who had defected to the United States. Reagan did raise this issue, and the Soviets relented, but The Brink of War makes it seem as if reaching agreement on this opened the way to more deals later. The movie ends with Reagan doubling back to try one more time on the Rostropovich issue. Gorbachev agrees, the men shake hands, and the last word of the movie is deal . This is not remotely what happened. According to Adelman, it was Gorbachev, not Reagan, who tried one more time to engage—and not on Rostropovich’s sister but on a nuclear deal. “Can’t we do something about this?” the Soviet leader asked as Reagan got ready to leave. “It’s too late,” Reagan said, and walked out. [ Read: How Hollywood taught a generation to fear the bomb ] In the movie, this coldly enraged Reagan is replaced by a smiling dealmaker who is deeply introspective. In a private moment, he stares at the scar from the 1981 attempt on his life; that night he has a fit of PTSD about the shooting as he tosses and turns. The next day, Reagan emphasizes to Gorbachev that he felt that God had spared his life for a great purpose. Whether Reagan had PTSD from nearly being murdered is a matter of speculation, but he said no such thing to Gorbachev. The movie is full of lines that sound good from Reagan but that he never said. At one point, he invites Gorbachev to “tear down this wall between us,” as if he were already thinking of the line he would use in front of the Berlin Wall a year later. Nor did he say to Gorbachev that the Soviet people were “pissed off” at their government, a line that rings especially false from Reagan, who did not approve of any kind of swearing. As Boot noted to me, the president would not even spell out the word hell in his own diaries. All of this is unfortunate, because Reykjavik was a crucial step in ending the Cold War, and The Brink of War could have captured Reagan’s admirable toughness and confidence without exaggerating either the president’s abilities or what happened in Iceland. Reagan deserves great credit for making the end of the Cold War possible not only by holding fast to his belief in the superiority of the American system but also by having the vision to see that the Cold War and its endless nuclear tensions did not need to be accepted by either side as an immutable fact of life. He came into office excoriating the Soviets, and learned—almost too late—that he had succeeded too well in scaring the Kremlin and had brought the world closer to war. Encouraged by Shultz and Nancy, he changed course during his first term, and he found a courageous partner in Gorbachev. Yet Reagan, especially at Reykjavik, was hobbled at times by rigidity and tunnel vision. At the summit, he tried to lecture Gorbachev on the bankruptcy of Marxism-Leninism—this did not go over well—and the president’s obsession with SDI tanked what might have been the most dramatic arms agreement in history. Gorbachev, too, was intransigent, but by Soviet standards he was practically a radical. Fortunately, Gorbachev would drop his objections to SDI in time for both men to sign a landmark treaty in 1987 that abolished all intermediate range nuclear arms in Europe and made the entire world safer. (Donald Trump foolishly withdrew from this treaty in 2019.) Reagan did not win the Cold War alone, but he and Gorbachev made the end of the conflict and a more secure world possible. The Brink of War , whatever dramatic license it takes, underscores that Reykjavik was part of that story. The summit itself turned out to be a failure, but Washington and Moscow later climbed over its wreckage to reach new agreements. Reykjavik did not end the Cold War, but the Cold War could not have moved toward its peaceful ending without Reykjavik and the spirit of discussion it fostered.

items.title: Burkina : Le Magistrat Issa Gouo officiellement investi dans ses fonctions d’Agent judiciaire de l’État
items.description: Le Magistrat Issa Gouo, a prêté serment, ce vendredi 14 août 2026 à Ouagadougou, à l’occasion d’une cérémonie solennelle pour servir en tant qu'Agent judiciaire de l’État (AJE). Cet acte officiel marque une étape clé dans le début de ses fonctions, puisqu’il est désormais chargé de défendre les intérêts de l’État et de ses démembrements devant les juridictions. Devant les autorités judiciaires et les acteurs du monde du droit, le nouvel AJE s’est engagé à mener sa mission avec intégrité, rigueur et dans le strict respect des principes régissant la représentation de l’État en justice. Sa nomination répond à la nécessité de renforcer la défense des intérêts publics dans les contentieux nationaux. Lors de la prestation de serment, debout et la main levée, Issa Gouo a prononcé la formule rituelle : « Je jure de bien et loyalement défendre les intérêts de l’État, d’exercer mes fonctions avec dignité, conscience et probité ». Une promesse qui scelle son entrée en fonction et son engagement au service de l’institution judiciaire. Le magistrat Issa Gouo (Matricule 130 493 L) a été nommé Agent judiciaire de l’État lors du Conseil des ministres du Burkina Faso du jeudi 30 juillet 2026. Il avait occupé le poste de Président du Tribunal de grande instance de Pô. Minute.bf

items.description: Le rappeur guinéen Le Mélangeur se produira pour la première fois au Stade Petit Sory de Nongo, le 17 octobre 2026, à l’initiative de la structure Events Loisirs. L’annonce a été faite jeudi 13 août, lors d’une conférence de presse réunissant des acteurs culturels, des journalistes et des fans. À cette occasion, Certifguinée a remis à Le Mélangeur un disque de platine, en reconnaissance de son parcours musical. La cérémonie coïncidait également avec son anniversaire. Très enthousiaste, l’artiste a invité ses fans, notamment les « Djanbar », à se mobiliser : « J’invite tous les Djanbar à venir ce jour, on va écrire l’histoire ensemble. On fera le meilleur concert inch’Allah. » a lancé l’auteur du tube « khamè Nana ». Pour Dj Five, attaché de presse de l’événement, le choix de l’artiste repose sur sa longévité et sa capacité à transmettre des messages à travers sa musique : « Donc, il n’est pas donné à tout le monde aussi de se stabiliser et de cartoner durant longtemps. […] Parce que tout simplement, en l’écoutant, nous constatons une éducation, une création. En l’écoutant, il y a de la gravité. Et en l’écoutant, il y a une énergie. » Il a également appelé les médias à accompagner l’événement : « chers journalistes, on se confie à vous, humblement, pour que nous puissions faire du rendez-vous du 17 octobre un événement mémorable et historique. » Sur la sécurité, il assure : « En matière de sécurité, faut que vous sachiez que nous ne lésinons pas là-dessus. La loi du spectacle demande des règles et nous ne manquons pas à ça. […] nous travaillons avec une gendarmerie très crédible, une police responsable, une sécurité civile professionnelle, mais aussi la Croix-Rouge et d’autres accessoires concernant le troisième pour que ce concert soit un succès absolu sur le plan sécuritaire. Merci. » Concernant la capacité du stade, il précise : « Au stade Petit Sory, il y a un nombre que le stade impose à chaque organisateur. Donc, nous sommes en train d’étudier cette situation. Vous aurez quand même tous les détails dans la dernière conférence que nous allons organiser une semaine avant le concert, le 17. » De son côté, Ablaye M’Baye, directeur de Meurs Libre Prod, a salué l’initiative : « Et tout de suite, moi j’ai dit : “Ça c’est un bon projet” et c’est un projet qu’il faut accompagner parce que je connais l’artiste. En tout cas, je connais ses œuvres. Je connais aussi que c’est un hitmaker et, il sait parler au cœur du public. » Il appelle également le public à soutenir davantage les artistes guinéens : « Aujourd’hui, il est important que le peuple qui est très humaniste, qui est comme… donne beaucoup de force aux artistes de chez lui. Donne beaucoup de force à Mélangeur. C’est ce qui va lui permettre d’aller à l’international. » Confiant, l’auteur du titre « gongoli » affirme : « Le stade, moi je suis pas inquiet, il va le remplir de toute façon, il sait ce qu’il vaut aujourd’hui. Mais il faut le pousser afin qu’il arrive sur l’international, et ça, ça passera par vous. » Présent à la conférence, Moussa Fofana, directeur général du BGDA, a souligné l’importance économique de l’événement : « Notre présence a un double sens. Le premier signifie qu’on est près des créateurs de la Guinée. Et on est content lorsqu’il y a toujours l’économie circulaire autour de la créativité. » Il estime que les événements culturels génèrent également des emplois et des revenus : « Il y a de l’argent dans la création artistique. Il y a de l’employabilité sur ces concerts. Les gens vont avoir du job ne serait-ce que pour un jour. Autour de ce concert, nos mamans qui vendent autour du stade, les disquaires vont avoir une économie augmentée. Les taxis-motos vont avoir une économie augmentée, ne serait-ce que pour le jour ! Le transport va sentir. » Enfin, le directeur général du BGDA a assuré de son accompagnement : « Nous vous accompagnons, la structure organisatrice de cet événement. Nos félicitations ! Mélangeur au stade, nous vous souhaitons très belle carrière. » Le rendez-vous du 17 octobre au Stade Petit Sory de Nongo est ainsi présenté comme une étape majeure dans la carrière de Le Mélangeur et un événement important pour le hip-hop guinéen. Mayi Cissé L’article Conakry : le Mélangeur vise le Stade Petit Sory pour ses « Djambar » le 17 octobre est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Maférinyah : un gardien assassiné dans les locaux d’une entreprise
items.description: L’insécurité suscite de vives inquiétudes dans la sous-préfecture de Maférinyah, où un homme a été retrouvé mort dans son lieu de travail dans la nuit du jeudi 13 août 2026. La victime, identifiée sous le nom d’Ibrahim Sylla, était gardien au sein de la compagnie chinoise Geo Engineering, implantée dans le district de Fandié, secteur Terrain. Selon le secrétaire général de l’entreprise, Ibrahim Sylla aurait été violemment agressé par des individus non encore identifiés. Il aurait reçu un coup de machette à la nuque avant de succomber à ses blessures sur place, aux environs de 22 h 30. Ce meurtre relance les inquiétudes liées à la sécurité dans la zone. Les circonstances exactes du drame ainsi que l’identité et les motivations des auteurs restent, pour l’heure, à déterminer. Face à cette situation jugée préoccupante, des appels sont lancés aux autorités compétentes afin de renforcer les dispositifs de sécurité dans la localité, d’identifier les responsables de cet acte et de les traduire devant la justice. Une enquête devrait permettre de faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire. Nous y reviendrons.

items.title: Religious diversity must not become a source of conflict – Peace Council
items.description: The National Peace Council has urged Ghanaians to protect the country’s religious diversity and ensure that differences in faith do not become a source of conflict, stressing the need for dialogue, tolerance and peaceful coexistence. Speaking on behalf of the Chairman of the National Peace Council, the Executive Secretary of the National Peace Council, George Amoh, said Ghana’s diversity should be treated as a strength and not a weakness that could be manipulated to destabilise the country. He was speaking at an engagement between the Inspector-General of Police and religious leaders at the Police Headquarters in Accra on August 14, following recent incidents that heightened religious tensions. Mr Amoh commended the Police for their swift intervention, saying the response demonstrated the importance of state institutions having the capacity to contain situations before they develop into serious conflicts. He, however, stressed that the country must not assume that recent developments would be the last test to its peace. According to him, disagreements and acts of deviance are inevitable in every growing society, but Ghana must have effective mechanisms to manage them whenever they occur. He said the answer to provocative or violent conduct should never be more violence. “Violence cannot be used to respond to violent conduct,” he said, urging citizens to rely on dialogue and lawful processes to settle grievances. Mr Amoh said Ghana had successfully brought together people of different religions, languages and cultural backgrounds under one nation. He said this diversity was reflected in the country’s democratic institutions and constitutional arrangements and should continue to serve as a basis for unity. He urged Christians and Muslims to recognise that their differences do not prevent them from sharing a common national identity and responsibility to protect Ghana’s peace. He stressed that protecting Ghana’s peace required collective responsibility from the Police, religious leaders, state institutions and ordinary citizens.

items.title: Accra Academy @ 95: Old Boys set to celebrate heritage with grand float and homecoming
items.description: The Accra Academy Old Boys Association will, on Saturday, August 15, hold a special float and homecoming to mark the school’s 95th anniversary and honour its four founders. The float will begin at 7 am from the Accra Academy campus, pass through parts of Accra, and make a stop at Ellen House in James Town, where the school began, before returning to the campus for the homecoming. Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Friday, August 14, Organising Secretary of the Accra Academy Old Boys Association, Alfred Mills, said the float was introduced as part of the anniversary celebrations to honour the school’s founders. “Because it’s our 95th anniversary, we introduced the float to honour the four founders of Accra Academy.” He said the float would also provide an opportunity to revisit the school’s origins at Ellen House, which was provided by Ellen Barker for the establishment of the institution. “It’s a pilgrimage that we’re going back to where it all began,” he said. Chairman of the Float and Homecoming Committee, Belo Cida Haruna, said the homecoming would also focus on supporting the school’s development. He said old boys would commission an Echo Park, a 12-unit ultra-modern washroom facility, and a six-unit classroom block as part of the celebrations. Mr Haruna said the projects demonstrated that the event was about more than reconnecting and celebrating. “It’s not just about going back to school, having fun, and taking part in all these activities. It’s also about giving back to the school and making a positive impact.” The float will pass through Kaneshie, Mamprobi Post Office, and James Town before continuing through Atta Mills Street, Adabraka Circle, and Obetsebi and returning to the Accra Academy campus. The celebration is expected to bring together old boys from different generations to commemorate 95 years of Accra Academy’s history and contribute to the school’s continued development.

items.title: Braces beyond treatment: Gen Z’s fashion craze and the hidden dental risks
items.description: Some years ago, spectacles became an unlikely fashion accessory among young people. Children would pester their parents for a pair, with some even pretending to have problems with their eyesight simply because they wanted to wear them. At the time, children who wore spectacles were often perceived as intelligent, affluent, or “dbee” [dada ba] and, depending on whom you asked, more attractive. The stereotype became so entrenched that spectacles were commonly associated with class prefects, school prefects, science students, and self-proclaimed serious students. Today, that craze has largely faded. Although some members of Generation Z still wear fashionable frames to enhance their appearance, attention appears to have shifted to dental braces. Braces are primarily used to correct orthodontic problems. Yet an increasing number of young people and even some middle-aged adults seem eager to wear them merely for aesthetic appeal, without necessarily having a dental condition that requires treatment. This raises an important question: Are there sufficiently stringent assessment and regulatory procedures to determine who genuinely requires braces, or has the practice been left to market forces and the demands of fashion-conscious consumers? Orthodontists and the relevant regulatory authorities are best placed to provide a definitive answer. Braces not accessories Dental braces are used to straighten teeth and correct orthodontic conditions such as crooked, crowded, or widely spaced teeth. They may also be prescribed to correct malocclusion, a condition in which the upper and lower teeth do not fit together properly when the mouth is closed. Braces work by applying gentle but continuous pressure to move the teeth gradually into their appropriate positions. Although they are commonly associated with children and teenagers, adults may also undergo orthodontic treatment where clinically necessary. There are several forms of orthodontic treatment, including traditional metal braces, ceramic braces, lingual braces, self-ligating braces, and clear aligners. The appropriate option depends on the nature and severity of the patient’s condition, as well as the recommendation of a qualified dental professional. Clear aligners are removable, unlike conventional braces, but they must generally be worn for most of the day to be effective. They are normally removed only when eating, drinking, brushing, or flossing. Orthodontic treatment often begins between the ages of nine and 14 because the jaw and facial bones are still developing and may respond more readily to treatment. This does not mean braces are ineffective in adulthood. Adults can also obtain good results, although treatment may sometimes take longer. Benefits of proper orthodontic treatment When prescribed and supervised by a qualified orthodontist or dentist, braces can significantly improve a person’s oral health and quality of life. Beyond producing a straighter smile, they can make the teeth easier to clean, reduce the risk of tooth decay and gum disease, and improve essential functions such as chewing and speaking. However, even properly prescribed braces may cause temporary discomfort, particularly after they are fitted or tightened. Patients may also experience irritation of the tongue, lips, or inner cheeks, difficulty eating, and occasional jaw pain. These effects are usually monitored and managed as part of professional orthodontic care. The critical point is that braces are not harmless decorations. They are medical devices designed to move teeth and alter a person’s bite. Their use should therefore be based on a proper clinical assessment, not simply a desire to follow a trend. Dangers of unsupervised braces Wearing braces without a genuine orthodontic need or obtaining them from an unqualified person can expose an individual to serious oral-health risks. Unnecessary or poorly controlled pressure may move otherwise healthy teeth out of position, creating gaps, crookedness, or a new bite problem. Other possible consequences include: tooth decay and permanent white or brown marks caused by plaque and food collecting around brackets; swollen or bleeding gums, which may progress to gum disease; gum recession and the loss of bone supporting the teeth; shortening of tooth roots because of unnecessary or poorly controlled pressure; damage to tooth enamel during the attachment or removal of brackets; cuts, mouth ulcers and irritation caused by wires or badly fitted components; infection from unsterilised instruments, unsafe materials or inappropriate adhesives; choking if a bracket, wire or decorative component becomes detached; jaw discomfort, difficulty chewing and headaches resulting from changes to the bite; injury to a tooth’s nerve, which may require root-canal treatment in severe cases; and The risk may be even greater where so-called fashion braces are fitted outside a properly regulated dental facility. Without an examination, X-rays where necessary, a diagnosis, and continuing professional supervision, there may be no reliable way of predicting how the teeth, gums, and supporting bone will respond. Is fashion worth the risk? It is difficult to understand why anyone would knowingly expose themselves to these risks solely for aesthetic satisfaction. Why pursue today’s fashionable appearance at the expense of tomorrow’s oral health?

items.title: RDC: 22 ans après, les banyamulenge commémorent le massacre de Gatumba
items.description: En République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), la communauté banyamulenge continue de réclamer justice 22 ans après le massacre de Gatumba. Dans la nuit du 13 au 14 août 2004, 166 membres de la communauté ont été massacrés dans un camp de Gatumba, au Burundi. Les banyamulenge accusent les rebelles burundais du FNL d’Agathon Rwassa d’avoir commandité ce massacre. Jeudi 13 août, plusieurs centaines de membres de la communauté banyamulenge venus de tout le Sud-Kivu se sont rassemblés à Bukavu.

items.title: Ayra Starr releases third studio album, ‘Starr Girl’
items.description: Nigerian singer, Oyinkansola Aderibigbe, popularly known as Ayra Starr, has released her third studio album titled “Starr Girl”. The 16-track project features Nigerian Afrobeats stars, Wizkid on “Gimme Dat” and Rema on “Who’s Dat Girl”. Other confirmed guest appearances include Kwn on “Amazing”, Theodora on “Ms. Paper” and Leon Thomas on “Pressure”. The album also includes previously released songs such as “Tornado”, “Hot Body” and “Where Do We Go”, alongside “Letter To God” and “Misunderstood”. This release marks another phase in Ayra Starr’s musical career as she continues to expand her sound and international profile. The album follows her debut studio album, “19 & Dangerous”, released in 2021, and her sophomore project, “The Year I Turned 21”, which was released in 2024. The singer has continued to build her profile internationally following the success of songs including “Rush” and “Commas”. items.title: Dr Moses Atinga targets grassroots rebuilding in Upper East NPP chairmanship bid
items.description: Medical doctor and New Patriotic Party (NPP) stalwart Dr Moses K. Atinga has unveiled a three-point strategy to rebuild the party in the Upper East Region as he campaigns to become Regional Chairman. Dr Atinga, who has served the party in various capacities over the years, argues that the NPP’s challenges in the region require stronger grassroots organisation, improved communication and a deliberate strategy for winning elections. His campaign is centred on what he calls the “Tripod Strategy”, comprising human resource and infrastructure development, effective public communication and electoral success. Experience from grassroots to regional level Dr Atinga is relying heavily on his experience within the party’s structures to make his case to delegates. He has served two terms as Assembly Member for the Zorko-Gambrongo Electoral Area in the Bongo District, one term as Bongo Constituency Treasurer and two terms as Bongo Constituency Secretary. He has also previously served as the NPP’s Upper East Regional First Vice Chairman. His supporters say the experience gained across grassroots representation, constituency administration and regional leadership gives him a strong understanding of the party’s organisational challenges. Dr Atinga has also positioned himself as a consultative leader who intends to build consensus among the different groups within the party. Three-point ‘Tripod Strategy’ Central to his campaign is a plan to strengthen the capacity of party officers at all levels, from polling stations and electoral areas to constituency and regional executives. Under the first pillar, Dr Atinga wants greater investment in the training and development of party officers, with the aim of building an organisation that remains active throughout the electoral cycle rather than mobilising only during election periods. The second pillar focuses on communication. He wants NPP communicators in the region to receive stronger training and support to articulate the party’s policies, achievements and positions more effectively. The strategy also seeks to develop a more coordinated and proactive communication system rather than allowing the party to operate largely in reaction to its political opponents. The third pillar focuses on elections and proposes a constituency-by-constituency assessment of the NPP’s recent performance. The approach would include targeted voter engagement, stronger mobilisation of young people and women, and closer monitoring of electoral trends at the polling-station level. Dr Atinga believes such detailed planning would help the party identify its weaknesses and develop specific strategies for constituencies where its electoral performance needs to improve. Unity central to rebuilding effort Dr Atinga has also made party unity a major part of his campaign, arguing that internal divisions have contributed to the NPP’s difficulties in the region. He maintains that supporters of rival candidates and factions should continue to have a place in the party after internal contests are concluded. His campaign is also advocating greater involvement of younger members in party organisation and leadership beyond their traditional role in election-season mobilisation. Under his proposed approach, experienced party members would mentor younger activists while creating opportunities for them to contribute their ideas, energy and skills to the organisation. Dr Atinga is presenting the upcoming regional chairmanship contest as an opportunity for delegates to determine the direction the NPP should take as it works to improve its electoral fortunes in the Upper East Region.

items.title: FIFA : le Maroc et cinq pays arabes renouvellent leur soutien à Gianni Infantino
items.description: Alors que Gianni Infantino fait face à une contestation grandissante au sein du football mondial, le Maroc et cinq autres pays arabes ont réaffirmé leur soutien au président de la FIFA. Une prise de position qui intervient après la pression exercée par plusieurs confédérations, notamment l’UEFA, la Concacaf et l’AFC. Gianni Infantino peut compter sur un nouveau soutien de poids. Les présidents des fédérations de football du Maroc, du Qatar, de l’Égypte, de la Mauritanie, du Liban et du Soudan ont exprimé jeudi leur « soutien total » au président italo-suisse de la FIFA. Dans une déclaration commune publiée par la Fédération égyptienne de football, les six dirigeants ont renouvelé leur confiance en la direction d’Infantino et salué son action à la tête de l’instance mondiale. « Nous exprimons notre plein soutien à M. Gianni Infantino, président de la FIFA, et renouvelons notre confiance en son leadership et son engagement continu en faveur du développement du football à travers le monde », ont-ils déclaré. Le Maroc réaffirme sa confiance Le Maroc figure donc parmi les six fédérations arabes ayant choisi de soutenir publiquement Gianni Infantino dans une période particulièrement mouvementée. Le Royaume, qui coorganisera la Coupe du monde 2030 avec l’Espagne et le Portugal, estime notamment que le président de la FIFA a contribué à développer les opportunités offertes aux différentes régions du monde. Les fédérations signataires ont également mis en avant les efforts d’Infantino pour renforcer le rôle du football comme moyen de rapprochement entre les peuples et les communautés. Elles souhaitent ainsi poursuivre leur coopération avec le président de la FIFA afin de développer davantage le football mondial et de renforcer la contribution du football arabe sur la scène internationale. Infantino sous pression Ce soutien intervient alors que la position de Gianni Infantino est de plus en plus contestée. Le président de la FIFA fait face à une vague de critiques après son projet, finalement abandonné, visant à permettre à des investisseurs privés d’acquérir des parts liées à la Coupe du monde. Plusieurs confédérations ont récemment accentué la pression. L’UEFA, la Concacaf et l’AFC ont notamment adressé cette semaine un message commun qui témoigne de leur opposition croissante à la gouvernance actuelle de la FIFA. Certains responsables souhaiteraient même voir Infantino quitter la présidence de l’instance mondiale. items.title: SEC blacklists 6 individuals, 3 entities for financing terrorism
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has directed capital market operators to freeze the funds, assets and other economic resources belonging to six individuals and three entities designated as terrorist financiers by the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC). The SEC, in a circular to all Capital Market Regulated Entities (CMREs) on Friday said the designations were made in line with the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022. The six individuals are Babangida Muhammed Adamu Hammajam, Abdullahi Umar Usman, Ibrahim Abubakar, Adamu Chiroma, Muktar Muhammad Adamu and Yakubu Ogirima Ibrahim. The three designated entities are Nine to Nine BDC Ltd, Generation Currency BDC Ltd and Abbal Bako & Sons Bureau de Change. According to the SEC, Hammajama was listed on June 18, 2026, for involvement in terrorism financing and support for the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), while Usman was designated for providing material support to a designated terrorist organisation through repeated financial transactions. The commission said Abubakar was listed for involvement in terrorism financing and membership of ISWAP, while Chiroma was designated for allegedly using Bureau De Change (BDC) operations and related corporate entities to facilitate the movement of funds linked to terrorist activities. Muktar Muhammad Adamu was listed on June 15, 2026, for providing financial support and facilitating transactions linked to the financing network of the ISWAP Okene cell, while Ibrahim was designated for providing material and financial support to the ISWAP Kogi cell. The SEC said the three entities were listed for their alleged involvement in facilitating and channelling funds connected to the ISWAP Okene financing network. The commission directed CMREs to immediately identify and freeze, without prior notice, all funds, assets and other economic resources in their possession belonging to the designated persons and entities. They are also required to report frozen assets and other compliance actions, including attempted transactions, to the Secretariat of the Nigeria Sanctions Committee. In addition, the SEC directed regulated entities to immediately file suspicious transaction reports with the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) for further analysis of the financial activities. It further instructed operators to report all cases of name matches in financial transactions as suspicious, whether occurring before or after receipt of the sanctions list. The regulated entities are also required to prohibit dealings with the designated persons and entities and continue monitoring for transactions involving them. The SEC said any findings should be reported to the Nigeria Sanctions Committee through its designated reporting channel. The circular takes immediate effect, with the commission warning that failure to comply would constitute a violation of the Investments and Securities Act, 2025, and the SEC Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Rules and Regulations. It said violations could attract regulatory sanctions, including fines, suspension of operations or revocation of registration. The SEC further reminded capital market operators that all unusual or suspicious transactions must be promptly reported to the NFIU. The post SEC blacklists 6 individuals, 3 entities for financing terrorism appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: An attack on Ghana’s peace is an attack on the future of its children — IGP
items.description: Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Christian Tetteh Yohunu has urged religious leaders to use their influence to prevent religious tensions and violence, warning that any attack on Ghana’s peace ultimately threatens the future of the country’s children. Speaking at an engagement with religious leaders at the National Police Headquarters on Friday, August 14, the IGP said religious leaders had a critical role to play in maintaining peace, particularly at a time when tensions could easily be inflamed by speech and actions. He stressed that citizens must not take the law into their own hands when they believe an offence has been committed, insisting that such matters must be reported to the appropriate state institutions. “No civilised society can survive when individuals take the law into their own hands. When a citizen believes a crime or an offence has been committed, the only righteous path is to report it to statutory authorities and trust the legal process,” he said. Mr Yohunu also emphasised the need to protect both freedom of religion and freedom of expression, while making it clear that those freedoms do not justify violence or unlawful attacks against individuals. “Every individual has a right to practice their faith without fear of violence,” he said. According to the IGP, although speech that incites religious hatred is restricted under Article 20 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), alleged offences must still be dealt with through lawful processes. “While speech that incites religious hatred is restricted under Article 20 of the ICCPR, due process and prohibition of extrajudicial harm, no suspect under state custody or in the public space may be subjected to torture, cruel treatment, or assault,” he said. Mr Yohunu, therefore, appealed to Christian and Muslim leaders to use their platforms to calm tensions and discourage their congregations, particularly young people, from resorting to violence. “Our revered clergy and the imams, our beloved chief imam, they listen to your sermons, read your social media posts, and follow your gestures,” he said. He warned that the influence of religious leaders could either help prevent conflict or worsen tensions depending on the messages they put out. “At this fragile moment, your words can either act as water upon an emerging fire or as petrol upon dying embers. I ask three key commitments from you today. Dedicate your Friday sermons in Islam and Sunday sermons strictly to messages of interfaith harmony, self-control, and the danger of religious conflict,” he urged. He also asked religious leaders to remind their congregations of the wider consequences of violence, particularly for future generations. “Remind your congregations that an attack on the peace of Ghana is an attack on the future of their own children,” Mr Yohunu said. He further called for visible cooperation between Christian and Islamic leaders as a way of demonstrating unity to the public and countering attempts to turn religious differences into sources of conflict. “ Let the public see Christians and Islamic leaders standing together, sharing meals, issuing joint statements, and walking through our communities hand-in-hand,” he said. The IGP said such cooperation was particularly important in reaching young people, who could be influenced by messages portraying religious differences as grounds for division. He urged religious leaders to teach their congregations that reporting alleged offences to the appropriate institutions, rather than seeking personal or communal retaliation, was consistent with both responsible citizenship and religious values.

items.title: DABOLA : le barrage hydroélectrique de Tinkisso à bout de souffle, la préfecture replongée dans le noir
items.description: Malgré la déconnexion stratégique des préfectures de Dinguiraye et de Faranah du réseau, le barrage hydroélectrique de Tinkisso peine toujours à alimenter la ville de Dabola. Entre la vétusté des équipements et la forte hausse de la demande locale, la crise énergétique s'aggrave, ce vendredi 14 août 2026. Entre des pannes à répétition affectant des groupes de production mis en service en 1970 et une surcharge globale dépassant la capacité nominale de 1,6 mégawatt (MW), les habitants de Dabola et de la sous-préfecture de Bissikirima restent privés d'électricité. « L’un de nos trois groupes de production est à l'arrêt, ce qui réduit drastiquement les capacités de la centrale. L’infrastructure est saturée et la demande surpasse désormais largement notre offre », explique Alpha Oumar Diallo, chef de la centrale de Tinkisso. Face à cette détérioration, les réactions d'inquiétude se multiplient sur le terrain. « C'est un cri du cœur de la population, car l'électricité et l'eau sont primordiales pour le développement d'une localité. Je me suis rendu sur le terrain pour évaluer la situation : force est de constater l'ampleur des difficultés. En réalité, la demande dépasse de loin l'offre et le matériel est particulièrement vétuste », a confié Colonel Alpha Oumar Cissé, le préfet de Dabola, après son constat. Pour sortir durablement de cette impasse, tous les regards se tournent désormais vers le projet d'extension « Tinkisso 2 », vivement attendu par les populations locales pour résoudre définitivement le déficit énergétique de la région.
